findings.claim: Uncertainty- and multiplicity-adjusted ranking differs from point-estimate ranking. Raw-covariance pair_kernel_1.5 and 2.5 have the largest whole-window means (8.70e-07, 1.70e-06) but their adjusted q-values are 0.134 and 0.116 with CIs spanning zero; the adjusted-covariance versions are the only pair-kernel entries with q<0.05 (0.081, 0.077) and CIs excluding zero, and endpoint_effects:9-12 show positive integrated z with positive_batch_fraction 1.0 for a=1.5,2.5,3.5. So a multiplicity-adjusted priority would rank pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 (adjusted) above the larger raw point estimates, and would not rank pair_kernel_5.0/7.0 highly despite nonzero raw means.

Joint/global diagnostics carry the strongest and most reproducible adjusted evidence: joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A have adjusted q of 2.8e-4 and 9.7e-4 (raw q 9.3e-5, 1.5e-4) with same-sign batch fractions 0.93 and 1.0, and joint_diagnostics:1 and :11 are the only joint entries with null_tested=true and q≈2.2e-9. joint_diagnostics:2 (observed_child_score_gain) is null_tested=true with negative mean and positive_batch_fraction 0.0, i.e. an opposing observation that weakens any claim that larger innovation/contrast uniformly improves the observed child score.

Local shape information is separable from global pose: global_centroid_x/y/z adjusted CIs all span zero (q 0.97, 0.86, 0.91), whereas shape_yy is the one shape entry with adjusted q=1.5e-5 (raw q=0.0026) and endpoint_effects:4 gives negative integrated z with positive_batch_fraction 0.0. The local_cyy regional field is negative and significant at every landmark (regional_effects:5,15,...,195, all q<0.005, positive_batch_fraction 0.0), while local_cxx is negative at most landmarks but not all. This supports retaining freedom in the local_cyy (and to a lesser extent local_cxx) extent around each landmark rather than in the global centroid.

Coherent joint patterns dominate isolated marginals: joint_internal_RMS_A (adjusted q=0.0014, same-sign fraction 0.93) and joint_innovation_RMS_A (q=6.6e-4) are far stronger than any single global_centroid or shape_xy/xz/yz entry, and joint_diagnostics:14 reports teacher_contrast_internal_fraction mean 0.787 versus translation 0.132 and rotation 0.081, i.e. the contrast is mostly internal rather than rigid. This is coupling evidence, not a license to average incompatible conformations into a target.

The soft_mass contrast curves are non-monotone across the observed support [0.0,0.49]: e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass rises from -0.37 to ~1.64 near t≈0.16 then falls to -0.28 at t=0.49, and landmark_10_soft_mass peaks ~1.03 near t≈0.05 then declines to -0.37. All continuous rows have extrapolation_allowed=false and polynomial_accepted=false, and curve_support's fidelity audit shows relative_node_rmse 0.58-0.93 with 0-15 strong sign-conflict nodes, so a constant rule is not supported over the full window and a time-conditioned rule would need validated fits rather than arbitrary bins.

The local_dx/dy/dz contrast curves show sign changes and rate reversals within the observed support (e.g. landmark_00_local_dy first_rate_z=-72.4, last_rate_z=+5.5, 6 sign changes; landmark_01_local_dz first_z=-0.90, last_z=-0.11 with 6 sign changes). Because these are observed-node linear interpolations with no accepted polynomial and no extrapolation, they are descriptive contrast curves, not absolute reward targets, and cannot be integrated into a single constant direction.

Population-contrast changes and parent-child increment contrasts diverge. For landmark_00_local_cxx the population_rate is -0.058 (q=0.91) while edge_rate is -4.34 (q=0.055) and turnover_residual_rate is +4.29 (q=0.038, positive_batch_fraction 0.86); similarly landmark_00_local_cyy population 0.26 (q=0.76) vs edge -4.79 (q=0.063) and residual +5.05 (q=0.033). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, so the evidence supports changing cohort composition and reclassification rather than a clean within-path change.

Survival (recorded joint-head) enrichment is weak and mostly not significant after BH: landmark_00_soft_mass survival_enrichment_z=0.365 (q=0.120) and landmark_10_soft_mass 0.234 (q=0.302), while the significant survival entries are negative local_czz/local_cyy terms (e.g. landmark_09_local_czz -0.390 q=0.120, landmark_05_local_czz -0.419 q=0.120). lineage_support states BH is joint over 400 survival field/measure tests and that these are not terminal affinity effects, so survival evidence should not be promoted to a coordinate rule.

The information audit reports compressed_choice_excess_fixed_RMS_A mean 0.081 (CI 0.070-0.092) and top4_teacher_overlap 0.470 (CI 0.427-0.515), with chosen teacher score correlations only 0.064-0.102; teacher_modes gives 28 teachers and assignment RMS quantiles 0.446/0.863/1.050 A. joint_diagnostics:4-10 (coherence 0.812, root_ESS 1.297, score_gap 0.172, noise 0.067, lower_rejected 0.326, expected_probability_advantage 0.007, sign_calibration_cosine 0.973) are descriptive within-selector associations, not null-tested. This bounds how much coordinate steering can be justified from teacher geometry alone.

Global centroid coordinates are not supported as a control direction: raw_covariance global_centroid_x/y/z have q 0.72, 0.69, 0.97 and adjusted_covariance versions q 0.97, 0.86, 0.91, with same-sign batch fractions 0.36-0.64; endpoint_effects:0-2 show integrated z near zero and mixed batch fractions. Any proposed direction on the global centroid would be weakened by these opposing observations and should not be prioritized.

Landmark 18 shows the most consistent adjusted landmark evidence: landmark_18_softmin adjusted q=0.059 (raw q=0.029) and landmark_18_occupancy5 adjusted q=0.038 (raw q=0.030), with same-sign batch fractions 0.79; regional_effects:380 and :389 give positive enrichment_change_rate_z for landmark_18_soft_mass (1.21, q=0.062) and landmark_18_local_cyz (3.03, q=0.018). This is a candidate region for a coordinate hypothesis, but the effect is on a softmin/occupancy descriptor, not a physical interaction energy.

Pair-kernel evidence is scale-dependent and not monotone: adjusted_covariance pair_kernel_1.5 and 2.5 are significant (q=0.081, 0.077) with positive batch fractions 0.79, while pair_kernel_3.5, 5.0, 7.0 are not (q 0.53, 0.45, 0.28) and pair_kernel_7.0 has negative integrated z (-0.485, positive_batch_fraction 0.0). A rule that increases all pair distances would be contradicted by the negative 7.0 A shell evidence, so any pair-kernel hypothesis must be scale-specific.

hypotheses.claim: Testable coordinate intervention: observable = adjusted pair_kernel_1.5 and 2.5 (radial pair-distance shell density at a=1.5,2.5 A, sigma=0.75 A); intended response = increase in the favorable-minus-comparison contrast for these shells; target origin = the executing pointcloud endpoint reward with pointcloud_delta_A=1.0 A; spatial scale = 1.5-2.5 A pair distances; temporal scale = whole window [0.0,0.5]; discriminating failure = if the adjusted pair_kernel_1.5/2.5 contrast does not increase while pair_kernel_7.0 contrast decreases, the hypothesis is falsified. This could be expressed by the registered pointcloud_delta_A edit (0.5/1.0/2.0 A) or teacher_neighbors edit (2/4/8), not by a pair-kernel term, which the executing scalar does not contain.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable = landmark_18_softmin and landmark_18_occupancy5 (normalized soft-min distance and radial shell density at landmark 18); intended response = increase in the favorable-minus-comparison contrast for these descriptors; target origin = the regional Gaussian landmark attention around landmark 18; spatial scale = core_radius_A=5.0 A around landmark 18; temporal scale = whole window; discriminating failure = if landmark_18_softmin/occupancy5 contrast does not increase, or if the same edit degrades landmark_00/landmark_10 soft_mass contrasts, the hypothesis is falsified. Expressible via the registered region_index edit (evidence-bound landmark) with pointcloud_delta_A in {0.5,1.0,2.0}.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable = soft_mass contrast curves at each landmark; intended response = a time-conditioned increase in soft_mass contrast during the early window (t<0.2) where the curves peak, without requiring a constant whole-window increase; target origin = the temporal_region recipe (same static teacher coordinates, only validated absolute contrast changes regional attention at actual score nodes); spatial scale = per-landmark core_radius_A=5.0 A; temporal scale = observed support [0.0,0.49]; discriminating failure = if the early-window soft_mass contrast does not increase, or if the late-window contrast decreases below its observed value, the hypothesis is falsified. Expressible via temporal_region_index and temporal_teacher_blend in {0.25,0.5,1.0}.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable = parent_edge_contrast_rate_z and turnover_residual_rate for local_cxx/local_cyy at landmarks 0,1,4,7,8,12,16,17,18,19; intended response = a within-path change in the local_cxx/local_cyy contrast that is not explained by cohort reclassification; target origin = the parent-child increment contrast; spatial scale = per-landmark local covariance extent; temporal scale = whole window; discriminating failure = if the turnover_residual_rate remains large and same-signed after the edit, the change is attributable to reclassification/parent weighting rather than within-path change, falsifying the hypothesis. This remains descriptive unless a registered recipe can express it.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable = joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A; intended response = reduction in joint innovation/internal RMS while preserving the observed child score gain; target origin = the joint contrast (teacher_contrast_internal_fraction 0.787); spatial scale = whole-molecule internal coordinates; temporal scale = whole window; discriminating failure = if joint_internal_RMS_A decreases but observed_child_score_gain (joint_diagnostics:2) does not improve or worsens, the hypothesis is falsified. Expressible via pointcloud_delta_A and teacher_neighbors edits, but the joint-motif term itself is not in the executing scalar.

Testable coordinate intervention: observable = shape_yy and local_cyy regional fields; intended response = increase in the favorable-minus-comparison contrast for shape_yy/local_cyy; target origin = the local covariance extent around each landmark; spatial scale = per-landmark radius_A=5.0 A; temporal scale = whole window; discriminating failure = if shape_yy/local_cyy contrast does not increase, or if global_centroid contrasts change in the same direction (which would indicate a rigid-motion confound), the hypothesis is falsified. Expressible via region_index and pointcloud_delta_A edits.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling; it is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis, and extrapolation_allowed is false for all continuous rows.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures; teacher score correlations are observational and not a validated affinity predictor.
All weak and null scalar effects are retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term; moment and pair-kernel effects are diagnostic only.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters; no temperature edit is proposed or permitted.
